questions.question: In cold temperatures, bridges usually freeze:

options.text: After other parts of the road.
Before other parts of the road.
At the same time as other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. Drive with extra caution on bridges and overpasses when it is cold and wet.

questions.question: After starting the engine, the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) light stays on if:

options.text: The ABS is working properly.
The ABS is not working properly.
The ABS is not engaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS light should come on when you start the engine, then turn off. If it stays on, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly if:

options.text: The trailer is straight.
There is no trailer.
The vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: For vehicles with trailers, you can only check mirror adjustment correctly if the trailers are straight. Always check your mirrors before you start your trip.

questions.question: Do not base your decision to shift gears on:

options.text: Your engine speed (rpm).
Your road speed (mph).
What other vehicles around you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What other vehicles around you are doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine speed or road speed. Learn your engine's operating range and shift up at the top of that range. You can also shift up based on your speedometer. Do not shift based on what other drivers do.

questions.question: The effects of alcohol are felt:

options.text: With the first drink.
Only after several drinks have been consumed.
At the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: With the first drink.
questions.explanation: Alcohol can affect you after your first drink. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while impaired by alcohol.

questions.question: If you must leave the roadway and drive on the shoulder in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Brake as hard as possible.
Get both sets of wheels onto the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.
questions.explanation: If you drive onto the shoulder to avoid a hazard, stay there until you stop. Then signal, check your mirrors, and merge back onto the road. Do not brake hard on the shoulder at high speeds. Keep one set of wheels on the pavement if you can.

questions.question: If you are backing and the trailer drifts off-course, you should:

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, correct it right away by turning the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.

questions.question: What does a shipping paper describe?

options.text: The materials being transported
How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.correctAnswerText: The materials being transported
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe the specific hazardous materials being transported, among other information.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Are illegal in most states.
Show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors.
Should replace flat mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are curved and show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, objects in convex mirrors appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What is a drawback of retarders?

options.text: They may not be allowed everywhere.
They can help slow a vehicle.
They cannot be turned off.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be allowed everywhere.
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow a vehicle and reduces brake use. However, retarders can be noisy and are not allowed everywhere.

questions.question: How does a truck's weight affect stopping distance?

options.text: It has no effect on stopping distance.
It is a major factor that affects stopping distance.
It is less important than the type of cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a major factor that affects stopping distance.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's weight greatly affects how far it takes to stop. Heavier vehicles need more braking power to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: When you brake suddenly, liquid in a partially filled tank can surge. What can this cause?

options.text: The truck to stop too quickly.
The truck to be pushed forward.
The truck to leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck to be pushed forward.
questions.explanation: When liquid surges in a partially filled tank, it pushes the truck in the direction of the wave. On slippery surfaces, this surge can push the truck forward into an intersection or another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you pay special attention to during a winter pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Coolant and antifreeze levels
The air conditioning unit
The oil pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Coolant and antifreeze levels
questions.explanation: During winter, check the coolant and antifreeze levels, defrosting and heating equipment, wiper blades, windshield washer, tires and tire chains, lights and reflectors, windows and mirrors, handholds and steps, radiator shutters, and exhaust system.

questions.question: If you discover a leaking tank, what should you do?

options.text: Try to fix the leak yourself by welding it closed.
Get the leak fixed right away.
Drive with flashers on to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get the leak fixed right away.
questions.explanation: Transporting liquids or gases in a leaking tank is illegal and unsafe.

questions.question: Are pre-trip inspections required?

options.text: They are recommended.
They are needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.
They are required by law.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required by law.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip, no matter how long or short.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
In the truck's manual.
In the Periodic Table of Elements.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
questions.explanation: The Emergency Response Guide (ERG) from the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) contains information about hazardous chemicals. It is organized by chemical names and identification numbers.

questions.question: If your tank vehicle spills, who may have to pay for cleanup?

options.text: You may have to pay for cleanup costs.
You are not responsible if someone else loaded the tank.
You must notify the local conservation department.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to pay for cleanup costs.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to transport liquids or gases in a leaking tank. If you do, you may be responsible for paying the costs of cleaning up the spilled material.

questions.question: During a truck fire, what should you do before opening trailer doors?

options.text: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.
Throw water on the doors.
Find someone else to open them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.
questions.explanation: Before opening trailer doors during a fire, feel them to check if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. If so, keep the doors closed because opening them could make the fire worse by giving it more oxygen.

questions.question: During an inspection, you should check all of the following except:

options.text: Whether your tires have too much air pressure.
Whether your tires have too little air pressure.
Whether all your tires are the same brand name.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether all your tires are the same brand name.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that tire air pressure is not too high or too low. Tire brand name does not need to be the same across all tires.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, what should you do?

options.text: Stay as far away from the flames as possible.
Aim directly at the flames.
Use any extinguisher on any type of fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away from the flames as possible.
questions.explanation: Stay as far away from the fire as possible. Aim at the base of the fire, not at the flames. Use the right type of extinguisher for the fire type. If you are unsure, wait for trained firefighters.
